newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour appoints Taylor to head anti-drugs fight.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour appoints Taylor to head anti-drugs fight.

text.p: Britain's new Labour government on Monday appointed Ann Taylor to head the battle against drug abuse.
Taylor, Labour's parliamentary business manager (Leader of the House), will chair a cabinet committee on drug abuse, Prime Minister Tony Blair said in a statement.

"I want to breathe new life into the battle against drugs. I want to draw together all parts of the community to work together against this modern evil. We will hit hard on drugs and on the drugs trade," said Blair.
The anti-drugs plan will run in tandem with a strategy to deal with lack of educational opportunity, homelessness and social decay.
Labour has already announced plans to appoint a high profile "drug czar" to lead the fight against drugs. Taylor will lead the search for a suitable candidate.
Taylor is married and has two children. -- London
